title: HB2198 (2025-2026 Regular): Enacting the gun violence restraining order act to authorize the issuance of protective orders prohibiting the acquisition and possession of firearms by certain individuals.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Kansas) (gun-policy Stage 5, Kansas); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Kansas text (Introduced; official copy, https://www.kslegislature.gov/b2025_26/bills/download/?apn=b2025_26/year2/ready_for_publication/hb_2198/hb2198_00_0000.pdf)
provenance.note: As filed (Introduced); no passage vote recorded. Order may be issued without notice (Sec. 3(c)) and extended in one-year steps (Sec. 8(a)); sections 5-7 set service and seizure procedure. Section 2's list is cut short in the quote (items 5-7 omitted).

operative_text:
Section 1 (new law): (a) Sections 1 through 8, and amendments thereto, shall be known and may be cited as the gun violence restraining order act.
Section 3 (new law): (a) In an action under section 2, and amendments thereto, the court may issue a gun violence restraining order if the court determines that there is reasonable cause to believe that the defendant poses a significant risk of personal injury to self or others by possessing a firearm.
Section 4 (new law): (a) If the court determines under section 3, and amendments thereto, that a gun violence restraining order is to be issued, the court shall include all of the following provisions in the order: (1) That the restrained individual shall not purchase or possess a firearm; (4) an expiration date that is not more than one year from the date of issuance. (b) In the discretion of the court, a gun violence restraining order may include an order to a law enforcement agency to seize firearms in the possession of the restrained individual.
Section 2 (new law): (a) Any of the following individuals may file an action with the district court requesting the court to enter a gun violence restraining order pursuant to the gun violence restraining order act: (1) The spouse of the defendant; (2) a former spouse of the defendant; (3) an individual who has a child in common with the defendant; (4) an individual who has or has had a dating relationship with the defendant;
Section 8 (new law): (b) An individual who refuses or fails to comply with a gun violence restraining order is subject to the criminal contempt powers of the court.
